text.text: Enzo's is a pretty popular and busy family restaurant. It is also pretty huge and surprisingly, we were seated immediately. Our food did take some time to get to us but considering the sheer amount of people in the restaurant, the wait time was still tolerable. Enzo's is a pretty good Italian-American restaurant. If you're looking for authentic Italian, this restaurant may fall a bit short. First of all, the portions are American sized. It's much more than the typical 60-100g of pasta. I ordered the penne pesto and the flavors were good. It had parsley, olive oil, some pine nuts and cheese. I wish the flavor of the pesto had been a bit nuttier but it was still good overall. Unfortunately, the pasta was a bit overcooked. My partner ordered the pollo allo scarpariello which is a rustic Italian-American dish. Entrees can be served optionally with your choice of pasta for $5. This was a fun way to add carbs to our meal :) the flavors were good and the potatoes in the dish were really tasty. Despite the chicken being covered in a delicious sauce, the outer layer of the chicken was still a bit dry and tough to chew. As you can see, the portion was also pretty big. We're open to try other dishes at Enzo's because we have seen good reviews.

This is Italy away from Italy! We celebrated my husband’s birthday with lunch and came here from out of state as we heard so much good about this restaurant’s authenticity and atmosphere. The food was exceptionally good, especially the Mafalde in Cartoccio, Insalata di Arugula, and Pasta Al Forno. The Mafalde was perfect—the best pesto I’ve ever tasted!

The staff were highly professional, knowledgeable, and friendly and we appreciated the birthday song for my husband.

The atmosphere was Italy itself and it could not have been more perfect. There was a separate bar area, back dining room and side dining room with a skylight.

My husband is half-Italian and also a former server at Commander’s Palace and now at a higher-end Italian restaurant in our hometown. He was over the moon with the exceptional quality and taste, especially the affordability and lack of artificial stuffiness.

This truly felt genuine and warm, which is everything we had hoped for. Thank you for a fantastic experience! 100% recommend!

text.text:
Another visit to Trattoria Zero Otto Nove, because some traditions are non-negotiable.

Ms. J. and I do the New York Botanical Garden first and then reward ourselves properly with pasta. As one should.

I ordered the Pasta al Forno, which showed up hot, cheesy, and very much not interested in being subtle. Comfort food doing the absolute most -- baked, sauced, and bubbling like it knew it was the right choice. One would think "Boiled eggs in pasta?", but trust me, the bechamel sauce takes it to the next level.

Ms. J. went for the daily special: Radiatori in Cartoccio, cooked inside a sealed pocket of aluminum foil and opened tableside like a little pasta reveal. Steamy, aromatic, and frankly a bit of a showoff -- in the best possible way.

And then there was the Tiramisu.
We shared it (heroically), and I'm just going to say it: top-tier tiramisu. Not too sweet, beautifully balanced, rich without being heavy -- one of the best we've had in NYC, and we do not make that claim lightly. We both love tiramisu. We both judge tiramisu. This one passed with stars.

Zero nonsense, big flavors, and a tradition that continues to age very well.

We'll be back. Obviously.

I think I officially found my new seafood spot! My boyfriend took me to City Island Lobster House over the weekend, and the food AND service were easily a 5/5. Our waiter Antonio was an absolute delight and took great care of us!

Fair warning, this place gets PACKED, so be prepared for a wait. But I loved that as soon as something was ready, they brought it right out everything arrived HOT and fresh.

I mean… you can’t go to the Lobster House and not get lobster! I ordered the Lobster Clam Bake Special with Maine lobster, mussels, baked clams, corn, clam chowder and dessert. The portions were generous and it was a great value for the amount of food you get. My boyfriend had the grilled Norwegian salmon, which was also REALLY good.

Now let me put you on: if you love garlic, GET THE NOODLES. The linguine in that garlicky olive oil sauce was SO good.

The antipasto and garlic bread they bring out beforehand are SO good, but consider yourself warned pace yourself! We made the rookie mistake of going in a little too hard and were already getting full before our entrées arrived.

Fresh seafood, generous portions, hot food and wonderful service. Pictures speak louder than words, so I’ll let the food do the rest of the talking.

Will absolutely be back!

text.text: This is our favorite restaurant for outdoor dining (and good seafood!) Located on the left when you enter City Island, it takes you away from the madness of the city. We've been coming here literally for deacdes, and it never disappoints. Nautically-themed throughout, you feel like you could be at a favorite local spot on the Cape. The servers immediately place a wonderful salad with balsamic vinaigrette, fresh garlic bread and a cheese plate on the table, all complimentary. Today, Earl was our waiter, and he was super friendly and couldn't be more helpful, as he got our drink orders in quickly. Their ultimate margarita is quite good, and I love their Frankenstein (a blend of 5 rums and fruit juice). Their twin lobster tail is outstanding (I always take home one as there's no way to eat it all!), and comes with baked potato. If watching your calories, the grilled filet if sole is a very good choice. All their seafood is fresh and cooked however you like it (grilled, broiled fried). The restaurant is very large, and their outside deck is coveted in good weather so get there early for lunch or dinner. The deck looks out upon a marina on Long Island Sound, with Orchard Beach to the north. It's so peaceful having your meal there, enjoying the breeze off the water. It's our happy place in the summer!

I chose this restaurant for Father's Day because I had such a wonderful experience here previously while celebrating my grandparents' 80th birthday. Unfortunately, this visit was the complete opposite.

While we were seated promptly for our 4:30 PM reservation, the service quickly went downhill. Our server was consistently dismissive and rude, from making condescending comments when we asked a simple menu question to rolling his eyes when my brother tried to place a to-go order. We waited approximately 90 minutes for our entrées, which I understand can happen on a busy holiday, but what was unacceptable was the lack of communication and the fact that we had to repeatedly flag our server down for drink refills and updates.

At one point, the server told us our food was delayed because we had "chosen to come at the busiest time," despite having a reservation. Management was aware of the delay but never came to our table to address the situation. The restaurant also appeared poorly maintained, with dirty dishes piled near our table and no effort made to properly clear our table throughout the meal.

The final straw came when our leftovers were being packed up and dirty plates were stacked on top of food we were taking home. When my father questioned it, the busser simply replied, "That's how we do things here."

As someone who spent five years managing an upscale Italian restaurant and continues to work in the hospitality industry, I understand that holidays can be challenging. Delays happen. However, professionalism, communication, and basic hospitality standards should never disappear because a restaurant is busy.

This was easily the worst restaurant experience my family has had, especially disappointing given how much we were looking forward to celebrating Father's Day here. Unfortunately, we will not be returning.

The Bronx Public — Brunch Done Right

The Bronx Public is a fantastic local bar with a strong brunch offering. The staff is attentive, portions are generous, and the experience feels relaxed not rushed.

Standouts:
•	Homemade biscuits, served warm with raspberry or strawberry butter are absolutely delicious.
•	$50 brunch menu includes your brunch entrée plus 1.5 hours of unlimited drinks (sangria, mimosas, or tequila sunrise).
•	I ordered a coconut martini on top of that smooth and so good.
•	DJ kept the energy up, playing all the jams without overpowering conversation.

Operational notes (the practical stuff):
•	They don’t rush you, which is a huge win for brunch.
•	The restaurant doesn’t split checks, but the handheld machine makes it easy to split payments yourselves by card.
•	Tax and tip are included, so no surprises at the end.
•	Drinks were flowing consistently throughout the brunch window.

Bottom line: Great food, solid value, lively vibe, and a smooth payment process. I’d definitely go back again.

Food Review — Patricia’s, Bronx

Time to try Patricia’s in the Bronx. This restaurant has already made a strong name in the area, and it certainly didn’t disappoint us. The ambiance was warm, and we felt welcomed as soon as we stepped in.

We visited just before New Year’s, and the restaurant was at full capacity, yet everything ran smoothly. Our orders arrived on time, and the server was very attentive, always smiling and checking on customers.

The food was fresh, flavorful, and well presented. The soup portion was generous and comforting. The salad was perfectly balanced, not too salty, and the beets were tender and well cooked. The steaks were juicy, tender, and cooked exactly as ordered. I had the salmon, which was moist and flavorful, paired perfectly with fresh vegetables—light, healthy, and not heavy at all.

The pizza was light, not greasy, and very satisfying. Authentic Italian-style pizza, simple and delicious.

After seeing desserts served at nearby tables, we couldn’t resist ordering some ourselves, and they were delicious and a perfect way to end the meal.

Overall, it was a very good and memorable dining experience.

text.text:
Five stars all the way around! We crossed several states to visit Arthur Avenue and to celebrate my half Italian husband’s birthday. I could not have asked for anything more and our expectations were exceeded on every level. My husband will always remember his special meal and the meal was perfect: exceptionally tasty and creative. Having been both a server at Commander’s Palace and currently a server in a higher end Italian restaurant back home, he was in heaven and deeply impressed. The Spiedini in our salad was a unique touch that his chef at home was very interested to learn about.

Our server was fantastic and clearly explained the menu. The atmosphere is also something that truly transports you to Italy itself.

The chef’s dedication to his craft clearly comes through in the food. On top of it, Roberto’s is devoid of the artificial stuffiness and greedy price gouging that sometimes consumes successful establishments. It truly felt genuinely Italian and that is why we chose this restaurant.

I highly recommend eating here without any hesitation, and would 100% do so again. If only this was in our home state! Nevertheless, thank you for a truly memorable birthday for my husband and unforgettable experience for myself.
